subject: Post-call: Sanitization constraints, retention expectations & SLA asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dunham <alex.dunham@medihealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@medihealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Sanitization constraints, retention expectations & SLA asks

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Good to hear the priorities (telemetry for ops, strict PHI gating for any downstream storage, and a desire to keep short retention windows for request logs). Recap and requested clarifications below so we have a shared scope for the pilot: 

1) Scope we discussed
- Ingested request & response streams from your inference gateway (sampling ~100%)
- Header-level controls: ability to drop or hash trace identifiers and client-supplied headers (e.g., x-session-id) before write-to-log
- Full redaction rules for obvious PII in bodies (SSNs, insurance numbers) plus configurable regex rules you provide

2) Questions we need answered before a pilot spec
- Retention target: you mentioned 30 days as a goal but compliance wants 7 days for production. Which do we plan for the pilot?
- Are there any internal headers that must never leave your VPC (we can strip at the edge)?
- Will you need per-customer residency (EU/US buckets) or is single-us residency acceptable for now?

3) Deliverables we proposed
- PoC: streaming sanitizer that applies header minimization + configurable body scrubbing (2 weeks)
- Evidence pack: sample sanitized logs + audit checklist for SOC review

Next steps I suggest: Priya to confirm retention target and a short list (5) of headers we must drop/hash; we’ll share a short PoC plan and a sample input log template (attaching). I’ve attached a first-pass proposal and a sample request log to illustrate format.

Thanks — Hannah

--

Subject: Re: Post-call: Sanitization constraints, retention expectations & SLA asks

Thanks Hannah — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: Compliance is firm about 7 days for request/response logs containing any PHI. They will consider 30 days only for aggregated telemetry (non-PHI) with strict access controls. For the pilot, plan on 7 days for any event that might contain PHI.
- Headers: We will provide a short list but two that are immediate concerns are x-internal-trace and x-client-token — both must be hashed or stripped before leaving our edge.
- Residency: For now, single-us residency is acceptable; downstream we may require EU buckets for EU customers but this is a future ask.

Also, we have an internal Ops question: if we hash trace IDs at the edge, will Redwood still be able to join events for debugging across retries? If hashing is deterministic we should be okay — wondering how that interacts with your sampling/kv cache.

Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
MediHealth

Alex — quick technical notes on the trace-id hashing question so we keep the conversation concrete: 

- Deterministic hashing: we support deterministic HMAC-style hashing at the edge using a customer-provided key (or one managed in your KMS). That preserves joinability for debugging within the same key scope (hashed value is stable across events) but still ensures the raw id never leaves your environment.
- KV cache and sampling: Redwood’s runtime joins on tokenized session keys at inference time; the hashed trace id can be used as a stable join key for logs/observability if you choose deterministic hashing. If you enable sampling (e.g., 1% long-term retention), we will include the hashed id in sampled events so you can reconstruct flows for included traces.
- Redaction caveat: if you use regex-based redaction in bodies, please include representative samples — overly-broad regexes can accidentally remove context useful for quality debugging. We recommend a tiered approach: header minimization (mandatory) + body scrubbing with allowlists for fields we should preserve (request_id, model_version).

We can sketch config flags for the PoC: {edge_hashing: true, hash_algorithm: hmac-sha256, retention_days: 7, sample_rate: 0} — will turn this into a short YAML for the pilot doc.

Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
